gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a Qi2.2 25W vent charger such as the ESR OmniLock needs at least 35 W of USB-C input to reach 25 W, so the car's built-in USB port won't do it and you must use the included 12 V DC adapter, or that its clip fits only bladed vents (blades 10–32 mm wide, 1–4 mm thick) and does not fit bladeless, round or hidden vents.
standout_why: I compared against Apple Support 105047 (the en-us and en-ca versions are the cited pages, Published Date September 18, 2026). It covers only Apple's own MagSafe puck: which iPhone gets 25/22.5/20/15 W, the 30 W (15V/2.0A) adapter for the 25 W tier, and the 16e/11/X/8 non-MagSafe note. It does not cover third-party Qi2/Qi2.2 chargers, car chargers, iOS versions or vent types. ChatGPT's own answer says only that the UGREEN car mount 'Requires a suitable car USB-C power source'. It names no wattage and gives no vent-type exclusion, even though it asked the shopper 'Tesla / Other car with traditional air vents'. I could not open the Anker car-mount guide (HTTP 401) or the Macworld best-of list, so I can't rule out that they mention input wattage.
kit_items: Home stand: ESR CryoBoost 3-in-1 Magnetic Charging Station (25W, Qi2.2), US Plug. It is Qi2.2 25 W, it charges iPhone, Apple Watch and AirPods, and Macworld (Simon Jary) says it 'ships with a powerful 50W USB-C wall charger and cable', so no separate adapter is needed.

Car mount: ESR OmniLock Magnetic Car Charger (25W, CryoBoost, Air Vent). It is Qi2.2 certified, and per 9to5Mac (Bradley Chambers) it comes with a DC car adapter that has a 40 W USB-C port. That clears the 35 W minimum for Qi2.2, which a car's own USB port probably won't. It fits only bladed vents 10–32 mm wide and 1–4 mm thick.

Phone requirement: an iPhone 17/17 Pro/17 Pro Max/Air, or an iPhone 16-series model (not 16e) running iOS 26, to get Qi2.2 25 W. iPhone 12–15 still work but at lower speed. iPhone 16e has no MagSafe, and ESR's car-mount listing excludes SE, mini and 16e.
Case: a MagSafe or magnetic case thinner than 2 mm (ESR's limit on both products).
